why: see `rust:Executor::next_deadline_us` -- the host-loop time-out, through `nros_cpp_executor_next_deadline_us`. Out-parameter plus `Result` so an uninitialised executor is an error rather than a deadline; `UINT64_MAX` when nothing is scheduled. Microseconds in a `uint64_t`, not a `std::chrono` duration, because this surface is freestanding (decision D1). rclcpp has no counterpart: its executor always owns the thread it waits on.
